title: Çalhanoğlu reported out as Stuttgart come to San Siro
description: François Letexier of France will referee Inter against Stuttgart on Wednesday.
mast_alt: Nerazzurri Daily Edition No. 84, Tuesday, November 24, 2026 — Çalhanoğlu reported out as Stuttgart come to San Siro

blocks.html: Hakan Çalhanoğlu, the midfielder, will miss Wednesday’s game with Stuttgart, Sportmediaset reports. He has tests today. The club has named the referee for the game, and Cristian Chivu, Inter’s head coach, speaks at 8:30 AM ET.

paras: François Letexier of France will referee Inter against VfB Stuttgart at San Siro on Wednesday, at 3:00 PM ET, 21:00 CET. Dennis Higler of the Netherlands is the video referee.
Inter are 15th in the Champions League table with six points, one behind Stuttgart. They have won their last two games, 1–0 against Shakhtar and 3–0 at Feyenoord.

Chivu holds his press conference before Stuttgart today at 8:30 AM ET, 14:30 CET, at Appiano Gentile, Inter’s training ground. The squad trained there on Monday morning after the trip back from Bergamo.

blocks.h3: Eighteen Inter Women players on international duty
paras: Serie A Women stops for the international break, and 18 Inter Women players have joined their national teams. Irene Santi has her first call-up to Italy’s senior team.
Inter’s next league game is at Roma on Saturday, December 12, at 9:00 AM ET, 15:00 CET.

blocks.h3: Çalhanoğlu to miss Stuttgart and Genoa
paras: Sportmediaset reports that Çalhanoğlu will miss Stuttgart and both games with Genoa, in Serie A and the Coppa Italia. He hurt the back of his right thigh in Bergamo and has tests today. It adds that he could be out for at least three weeks.
Piotr Zieliński, the midfielder, has had a foot problem for about two weeks and is unlikely to play. The paper names Aleksandar Stanković, a midfielder, as the natural replacement.

Tuttosport, a Turin sports daily, reports that Çalhanoğlu’s contract runs to June 2027. It says his agent wants about €6.5 million a year for two more years, while Inter want a lower fixed salary with bonuses (Italian salaries are quoted after tax).
